title: Customer network interlock orchestration and self-serve lanes for Private/VPC/on-prem intake
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: create an operational playbook and automation lane that reduces hands-on engineering time for Private/VPC/on-prem customer network triage. The playbook covers: (1) automated preflight probes and self-serve checks customers can run before an engagement, (2) an interlock orchestration checklist that surfaces gating signals for upgrades and air-gapped rollouts, and (3) a set of communication templates and escalation lanes for high-risk networks. This ticket scopes the product requirements, acceptance criteria, and an initial implementation plan for a minimal viable 'Network Readiness Lane' that integrates into the intake flow.
background: We receive many non-bug requests for Private deployments where network constraints (e.g., proxy-only egress, strict firewall policies, limited upgrade windows, airgapped environments) drive engineering time. Current intake relies on manual email/Zoom triage and ad-hoc probes. This causes long time-to-onboard, unclear prioritization, and occasional late-stage blockers during upgrades. A repeatable, partially automated triage will improve throughput and reduce operator context-switching.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A documented triage rubric that maps customer-provided artifacts (network diagram, egress rules, proxy ACLs, certificate policy) to risk buckets (Green/Amber/Red) and recommended lanes (Self-serve / SRE-assisted / Engineering-assisted). 2) Automated preflight probe script (shell + Python) published in Drive and linked in onboarding emails; script returns machine-readable status codes and human-readable summary. 3) Intake UI checkbox + links to run probes with automatic ingestion of probe results into the ticket. 4) Communication templates for each lane (onboarding steps, expected time, required artifacts). 5) Pilot onboarding of 3 customers with different risk profiles and documented time savings and issues logged.
notes: Trade-offs considered: fully automated gating vs. lightweight human review; we prioritize a hybrid approach where automation reduces noise and surfaces edge cases for human review. Security: all probes must not exfiltrate sensitive data; default scripts use non-destructive checks (port/connectivity/HTTP handshake) and require customer consent. Metrics to track: time-to-first-successful-probe, time-to-ready, number of manual escalations, and engineer-hours per onboarding.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): Define rubric, templates, and basic probe scripts. Phase 2 (3 weeks): Integrate probe result ingestion into intake form and wire up ticketing labels and routing rules. Phase 3 (4 weeks): Pilot with three customers and iterate on false positives/negatives. Phase 4: Hand off to docs and playbooks team and bake into Console onboarding screens.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: probes mis-classify networks and create false confidence. Mitigation: include a 'confidence' score and require human review for low-confidence results. Risk: legal/regulatory objections to running probes. Mitigation: add explicit consent workflow and an offline/manual alternative. Risk: SRE/Eng bandwidth; Mitigation: reserve 2 engineer-days per week for runbook creation and pilot support.
